from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

                 "Average speed becomes instantaneous speed.", 
                 "Calculus reveals the truth of the moment."]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Velocity Analogy", lines)
        
        # Animation Elements

        slope_line = TangentLine(curve, alpha=0.4, length=1.5, color="#F3FF33")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(gauge_group, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Rotate(needle, angle=-PI/2, about_point=gauge.get_center(), rate_func=linear))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(gauge_group), FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)), 
                  FadeIn(curve))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Create(dot), Create(slope_line))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#F3FF33")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(slope_line.animate.scale(1.5))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Consider a simple curve.", 
            "Draw a secant line between two points.", 
            "Slide the second point toward the first.", 
            "The secant converges to a tangent line.", 
            "This line defines our instantaneous slope."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Visual: The Secant-to-Tangent Transition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define curve
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2 + 0.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # Grouped VGroup as per B002
        graph = VGroup(axes, curve)
        self.place_in_area(graph, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Points
        x1, x2 = -1, 1
        p1 = axes.c2p(x1, x1**2 + 0.5)
        p2 = axes.c2p(x2, x2**2 + 0.5)
        
        dot1 = Dot(p1, color=BLUE)
        dot2 = Dot(p2, color=RED)
        
        # Secant
        secant = Line(p1, p2, color="#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(graph))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(dot1), Create(dot2), Create(secant))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Use ValueTracker for smooth slide
        t = ValueTracker(x2)
        secant.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(
            axes.c2p(x1, x1**2 + 0.5), 
            axes.c2p(t.get_value(), t.get_value()**2 + 0.5)
        ))
        dot2.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(t.get_value(), t.get_value()**2 + 0.5)))
        
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(x1 + 0.1), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        secant.set_color("#33FF57")
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#F3FF33")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Core Concept: The Derivative as a Local Linear Transformer", 
                          ["Derivatives are local linear transformers.", 
                           "Magnify a curve to see a line.", 
                           "The derivative is the local magnification factor.", 
                           "It translates input variations to output changes.", 
                           "Linear approximation defines the derivative."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display linear transformation matrix acting on a vector
        matrix = Matrix([[1, 0.5], [0, 1]], left_bracket="[", right_bracket="]")
        vector = Matrix([[1], [0]], left_bracket="[", right_bracket="]")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(vector, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), Write(matrix), Write(vector))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate vector rotating and scaling
        vector_new = Matrix([[1], [0.5]], left_bracket="[", right_bracket="]")
        self.place_at_grid(vector_new, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5733"), Transform(vector, vector_new))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show 'Derivative' as the local Jacobian matrix
        jacobian_label = Text("Derivative = J", font_size=24, color="#33FF57")
        self.place_at_grid(jacobian_label, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"), FadeIn(jacobian_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Overlay local grid distortion to show linearity
        grid_square = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#F3FF33")
        self.place_in_area(grid_square, 'D3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#F3FF33"), Create(grid_square))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Fade in label 'Local Linear Map'
        label = Text("Local Linear Map", font_size=28, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'F3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), FadeIn(label))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Sensitivity: The 'What-If' Machine", [
            "The derivative is a sensitivity gauge.", 
            "It amplifies or shrinks input nudges.", 
            "Small input change leads to output shift."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        x_label = MathTex("x").set_color(WHITE)
        fx_label = MathTex("f(x)").set_color(WHITE)
        input_box = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE)
        output_box = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE)
        sensitivity_label = MathTex(r"\text{Sensitivity} = f'(x)").set_color("#33FF57")
        
        self.place_at_grid(input_box, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(x_label, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(output_box, "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(fx_label, "C5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        # Animate Nudge
        nudge = ValueTracker(0)
        input_box.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_stroke(opacity=1 - abs(nudge.get_value())))
        self.play(nudge.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=1)
        self.play(nudge.animate.set_value(0), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.place_at_grid(sensitivity_label, "E3")
        self.play(Write(sensitivity_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", ["Derivatives reveal linear truth in curves.", "We turn dynamic change into static ratios.", "Zooming in makes complexity manageable."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display summary table of derivative concepts
        table = Table(
            [["Concept", "Role"], ["Velocity", "Tangent"], ["Sensitivity", "Linearity"]],
            include_outer_lines=True
        ).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(table, 'A1', 'C6')
        self.play(FadeIn(table))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate connecting lines between 'Velocity', 'Tangent', and 'Linearity'
        v = table.get_cell((2, 1))
        t = table.get_cell((2, 2))
        l = table.get_cell((3, 2))
        
        line1 = Line(v.get_right(), t.get_left(), color="#FF5733")
        line2 = Line(t.get_bottom(), l.get_top(), color="#FF5733")
        
        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash the synthesized conclusion 'Derivative = Local Sensitivity'
        conclusion = MathTex(r"\text{Derivative} = \text{Local Sensitivity}", color="#33FF57").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, 'E3')
        
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.play(Indicate(conclusion))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57")
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: From Slopes to Sensitivities

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Velocity Analogy
sections.content: Begin by connecting the abstract derivative to a physical transformation. We move from measuring 'average speed' (change over a distance) to 'instantaneous speed' (the limit as the time interval vanishes).
sections.example: A cheetah chasing a gazelle: Instead of saying the cheetah ran 60mph total, we zoom in on the exact micro-second it lunges to capture the velocity at that precise point.

sections.title: Prerequisite Visual: The Secant-to-Tangent Transition
sections.content: Recall the slope formula (rise/run). Visually demonstrate a secant line connecting two points on a curve, then animate the second point sliding along the curve toward the first until they merge into a single tangent line.
sections.example: Visualize a roller coaster track; the 'secant' is a straight board connecting two peaks, while the 'tangent' is the exact tilt of the coaster car at a single point.

sections.title: Core Concept: The Derivative as a Local Linear Transformer
sections.content: Introduce the 'Transformational View': Instead of just a slope, define the derivative as a operator that transforms 'x' variations into 'y' variations. Zoom into a curve until it becomes a straight line; the derivative is the magnification factor of that local linear map.
sections.example: Imagine a smartphone screen. As you zoom in on a small section of a curved map, the curved road looks like a perfectly straight path. The derivative tells you how much your vertical position shifts for every 1 unit of horizontal movement.

sections.title: Visualizing Sensitivity: The 'What-If' Machine
sections.content: Reframe the derivative (f'(x)) as a sensitivity gauge. If I nudge 'x' by a tiny amount, how much does the output 'f(x)' amplify or shrink that nudge? The derivative is the scaling factor of the input change.
sections.example: A smart thermostat: If the derivative of temperature relative to power is 2, a 1% increase in power leads to a 2% change in heat output. The derivative is the 'knob' turning efficiency.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Conclude that the derivative is not just a calculation, but a 'zoom-in' tool that reveals the linear truth hidden within complex curves. It turns dynamic change into a static, manageable ratio.
sections.example: Final shot: A complex, swirling animation of a wave smoothing out into a single, perfectly straight arrow indicating direction and rate of change.
